# UDreamUIWidgetLibrary

<!-- Generated by the DreamGUIReferenceDocs commandlet from reflection. Edit the header, not this page. -->

Inherits from `UBlueprintFunctionLibrary`.

Declared in `Public/DreamUIWidgetLibrary.h`.

Finding widgets, driving a drag, and building an image brush from Blueprint -- the parts of
UMG's UWidgetBlueprintLibrary that mean something in this framework.

The parts that do not are named in the parity table with their reasons, and they are all one
reason: UMG's library is half Slate plumbing. FEventReply, the OnPaint drawing context and the
Slate input-event structs describe an SWidget's conversation with Slate, and a DreamGUI widget
never has that conversation -- its input arrives as a UDreamPointerEventData from the event
system and its pixels come from its own mesh.

| `bool CancelDragDrop(UObject* WorldContextObject)` | callable | End every drag in flight without a drop -- what Escape does. True when there was one to cancel. |
| `UDreamDragDropOperation* CreateDragDropOperation(TSubclassOf<UDreamDragDropOperation> InOperationClass)` | callable | Make a drag operation to hand to a drag that is starting -- UMG's CreateDragDropOperation. |

## Compared with UMG

Every Blueprint-facing member of the UMG class, and where it went. *adopt*: same name, same meaning. *map*: here under another name or on another type. *reject*: deliberately absent, with the reason.

| UMG | Member | Status | Here | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `UWidgetBlueprintLibrary` | `Create` | map | `UDreamUIBPLibrary::CreateDreamWidgetOfClass` | Pre-existing. AddWidgetOfClassToViewport is the create-and-show pair. |
| `UWidgetBlueprintLibrary` | `CreateDragDropOperation` | adopt | `CreateDragDropOperation` | Outered to the transient package, as UMG does: an operation outlives the widget that made it, and a recycled list row mid-drag is the ordinary case. |
| `UWidgetBlueprintLibrary` | `SetInputMode_UIOnlyEx` | map | `UDreamUIInputModeLibrary::SetInputModeUIOnly` | Addressed by DreamGUI user index rather than by a raw controller, so split screen does not have to rediscover which player a menu belongs to. |
| `UWidgetBlueprintLibrary` | `SetInputMode_GameAndUIEx` | map | `UDreamUIInputModeLibrary::SetInputModeGameAndUI` |  |
| `UWidgetBlueprintLibrary` | `SetInputMode_GameOnly` | map | `UDreamUIInputModeLibrary::SetInputModeGameOnly` |  |
| `UWidgetBlueprintLibrary` | `SetFocusToGameViewport` | adopt | `SetFocusToGameViewport` | A Slate focus change, not a DreamGUI one. UDreamWidget::ClearKeyboardFocus is the framework-level counterpart and the two are usually wanted together. |
| `UWidgetBlueprintLibrary` | `DrawBox` | reject |  | UMG's Draw* family writes into an FPaintContext handed to a Blueprint OnPaint override. There is no immediate-mode paint pass here: a DreamGUI widget draws by owning a mesh, so anything drawn is a widget with a visual on it rather than a call inside a paint. |
| `UWidgetBlueprintLibrary` | `DrawSpline` | reject |  | See DrawBox. |
| `UWidgetBlueprintLibrary` | `DrawLine` | reject |  | See DrawBox. |
| `UWidgetBlueprintLibrary` | `DrawLines` | reject |  | See DrawBox. |
| `UWidgetBlueprintLibrary` | `DrawTextFormatted` | reject |  | See DrawBox. |
| `UWidgetBlueprintLibrary` | `Handled` | reject |  | FEventReply is Slate's reply object, built by a handler and returned to Slate. A DreamGUI handler answers a bool meaning 'let this keep bubbling' (the IDreamPointer* interfaces), so there is no reply object to construct. |
| `UWidgetBlueprintLibrary` | `Unhandled` | reject |  | See Handled. |
| `UWidgetBlueprintLibrary` | `CaptureMouse` | reject |  | There is no capture to take: a pressed pointer's PressWidget already receives every drag and the release wherever the pointer travels. UDreamWidget::HasMouseCapture reports that state. |
| `UWidgetBlueprintLibrary` | `ReleaseMouseCapture` | reject |  | See CaptureMouse. |
| `UWidgetBlueprintLibrary` | `LockMouse` | map | `UDreamUIInputModeLibrary::SetMouseLockMode` | Separate from the input mode on purpose there: re-setting the whole input mode to change only the lock is how a project takes focus away from its own menu. |
| `UWidgetBlueprintLibrary` | `UnlockMouse` | map | `UDreamUIInputModeLibrary::SetMouseLockMode` | EMouseLockMode::DoNotLock. |
| `UWidgetBlueprintLibrary` | `SetUserFocus` | map | `UDreamWidget::SetUserFocus` | A verb on the widget rather than a reply built inside a handler. |
| `UWidgetBlueprintLibrary` | `ClearUserFocus` | map | `UDreamWidget::ClearKeyboardFocus` |  |
| `UWidgetBlueprintLibrary` | `SetMousePosition` | map | `SetMousePosition` | A verb rather than UMG's FEventReply builder. Viewport pixels, the same space GetMousePositionOnViewport reports and a geometry's absolute coordinates are in, so 'warp the cursor onto this widget' is one conversion and not two. |
| `UWidgetBlueprintLibrary` | `DetectDrag` | reject |  | UMG makes a handler arm drag detection for a key. Here the pointer pipeline detects drags itself against a distance and hold threshold (UDreamEventSystem's drag settings), so there is nothing for a handler to arm -- what a source supplies is the drag's MEANING, which is CreateDragDropOperation plus BeginDragWithOperation. |
| `UWidgetBlueprintLibrary` | `DetectDragIfPressed` | reject |  | See DetectDrag. |
| `UWidgetBlueprintLibrary` | `EndDragDrop` | reject |  | The pipeline ends a drag when the pointer is released; a handler has no reply to end it through. CancelDragDrop is the verb for ending one early. |

Not the same as a rect block's material, which belongs to the draw call and is deliberately not handed out (see Border.json). |
